_comment: Written by the Security Review persona. The pre-tag CI job reads this to decide whether a release is covered by a current audit. Do not hand-edit.
open_findings: MEDIUM #140: an uncovered release is easy to accept repeatedly, because no run knows what the previous run decided; and 'not verified' items live as prose with no lifecycle. OPEN and deliberately NOT accepted — see the acceptance note below.

MEDIUM #125: the client-side admin gate is a UX gate. Scope widened by v1.0.53: applyDetected() adds PUT /api/v2/apps/installations/{id} behind the same unprobed check. Both endpoints vendor-documented admin-only, neither probed by TSANet.
MEDIUM #96: durable audit trail. Strengthened by this review's probe showing Zendesk records nothing at all for ZIS registry writes.
LOW #98: note attribution heuristic remains open pending Connect-API-Code#131
notes: Extends the v1.0.53 review (originally recorded at c166008) forward to 724ec9d, which is that review's own remediation plus two docs commits. The findings count is unchanged because this is the same review, not a new one.

SELF-REVIEWED, and unusually so: this reviewer wrote most of the code under review, found the findings, and wrote their fixes. Weight accordingly; the 'clean' categories remain the weakest part of this record.

CLOSED BY THIS REMEDIATION: #138 (release.yml no longer interpolates ${{ github.ref_name }} into a run: block — the tag is bound in env: and referenced as "$TAG"; merged as 1a5f981) and #139 (the workflow-permissions rule now globs the directory instead of reading release.yml alone; merged as 724ec9d).

TWO NEW MECHANICAL CHECKS, both proven failing before being trusted. check_workflow_expression_injection() globs the workflow directory and FAILs on any ${{ }} inside a run: script — demonstrated by reintroducing the vulnerable line and watching it name release.yml:321. check_all_workflows_declare_permissions() globs and FAILs when any workflow lacks a permissions block — demonstrated by removing the block from zis-readme-check.yml, and separately proven to FAIL on an empty workflow directory rather than passing vacuously (#108's failure mode). Mechanical floor is now 14 PASS.

The two rules were split rather than merged: check_workflow_permissions() still reads release.yml alone, deliberately, because that workflow must be permissions:{} with jobs opting in, while contents: read is correct for the three read-only workflows. Both functions carry a note saying which is which, so the next workflow-wide rule lands in the globbing one instead of becoming a third narrow check.

SOURCE DRIFT since c166008, reviewed and inert: ec543ef (Shawn's quick-start merge) touched two watched paths — a remediation string literal in scripts/audit-connection-auth.py and two documentation links in zis/README.md. Diffs inspected; no logic and no security surface in either.

DOCS DEFECT found while verifying the quick-start merge, corrected on both surfaces: QUICK_START.md and the GitBook Installation Guide both stated that TSANet Action and TSANet Action Text 'are not covered by Detect field IDs' and told members to copy those IDs out of Admin Center URLs. Both fields are optional entries in EXPECTED_FIELDS in the shipped deploy.js, and Detect resolving and applying them was verified on DEV. Fixed in 3655fda and published to the live and sandbox GitBook spaces, with the public page re-fetched to confirm. Not a security finding, but it recreated exactly the toil #135 removed.

OBSERVATION, not a finding: a change to scripts/security-audit.py triggers no CI on a pull request, because no workflow path filter covers scripts/*.py other than lint-workflows.py. The audit runs pre-tag inside release.yml, so a broken audit script would surface at tag time rather than at review time. Worth considering alongside #140.

TAXONOMY: Category 1 gained a row for untrusted input reaching workflow shell, committed to tsanet-ops as 7065c7b. taxonomy_version raised 2 -> 3. The row exists because the checklist never asked the question, which is why three prior reviews passed over #138 — the same reason Category 7 was added after the first review missed XSS.

NOT VERIFIED, carried forward: (1) ZIS rejecting an agent-role session, and PUT /api/v2/apps/installations/{id} rejecting one — #125, blocked on an agent-role user existing on a sandbox. (2) The rewritten release gate's behaviour under a failing audit: logic read, not exercised. (3) #138 was reasoned rather than executed — the tag names were confirmed creatable and the substitution confirmed pre-shell, but no hostile tag was pushed, because that would run the injected code in CI. The fix is likewise verified by the new check rather than by exploitation. (4) That private apps do not auto-update.

ACCEPTANCE, and its consequence: accepted_issues carries forward only what a human has signed for (#96, #98, #119, #125). #138 and #139 drop off, closed. #140 is OPEN and deliberately NOT accepted, so the next tag will flag as shipping with an unaccepted finding. That is intended — this reviewer does not sign off on its own findings, and the persona may tighten a gate but never loosen one. #140 concerns the gate's own ergonomics and touches nothing in the shipped artifact, so accepting it is a reasonable call; it is simply not this reviewer's call to make. Add 140 to accepted_issues to ship without the flag.
The remaining mechanical WARN is the known v1-endpoint sunset 2027-01-01 (#101).
